subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: 'White space' (negative space) in a layout is...
options: The empty areas that help organise and balance a design
A design fault to be avoided
questions.explain: White space is the empty area around elements that gives a layout clarity and balance.

options: The art of arranging type and lettering
questions.explain: Typography is the design and arrangement of type so that text is legible and appealing.

questions.q: Why is knowing the 'target audience' important in a design?
options: It shapes style, tone and content to suit who the design is for
It decides the price of paint
It has no effect on the design
It is only needed for sculpture
questions.explain: Understanding the target audience guides the style, language and imagery so the design appeals to them.

questions.q: In graphic design, what does 'layout' mean?
options: The arrangement of text and images on a page
questions.explain: Layout is how text, images and space are arranged on the page or screen.

questions.q: A serif font is one that has...
options: Small lines or 'feet' at the ends of letters
questions.explain: Serif fonts have small finishing strokes (serifs) at the ends of letters; sans-serif fonts do not.

options: A drawn or painted image made to explain or decorate
A photograph taken with a camera
questions.explain: An illustration is a created image that supports, explains or decorates a piece of communication.

questions.q: Red is often chosen in branding to suggest...
questions.explain: Red carries strong associations of energy, excitement and urgency, useful for grabbing attention.

questions.q: 'Packaging' design must do all of these EXCEPT...
questions.explain: Packaging protects, informs and attracts, but it does not replace the product it contains.

options: The client's requirements and the target audience
questions.explain: A design brief defines the task, the client's needs and the intended target audience.

options: A symbol or mark that identifies a brand
A full page of body text
questions.explain: A logo is a distinctive symbol or wordmark used to identify and represent a brand.
